title: Hearing the Law, Then Celebrating
overview: The returned exiles gather to hear God's Law read and explained, weep at what they hear, are told to celebrate instead, and then joyfully keep the Festival of Shelters.

parts.label: The people ask for the Law (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The first day of the seventh month was already a sacred day marked by trumpets, and the people themselves asked Ezra to bring out the Law and read it in a public square by the Water Gate. Men, women and anyone old enough to understand stood listening from dawn until noon.

parts.label: Ezra on the platform (vv. 4-6)
parts.note: Ezra stood on a raised wooden platform so everyone could see and hear, with thirteen leaders beside him, probably to show their support and to share the long reading. Standing, lifting hands, saying "Amen" (meaning "yes, so be it") and bowing low were ways of showing deep respect for God and for the words about to be read.

parts.label: Making the meaning clear (vv. 7-8)
parts.note: Levites, members of the tribe that assisted the priests, helped the crowd understand what was read. Scholars are unsure whether this meant translating the Hebrew into Aramaic, the everyday language many exiles now spoke, or explaining its meaning, and it may have been both.

parts.label: Tears turned to feasting (vv. 9-12)
parts.note: The people wept, most likely because the Law made them see how far they and their nation had fallen short. Their leaders told them this was a holy festival, a day for good food and for sending portions to those who had nothing, because the joy of the LORD would be their strength.

parts.label: Rediscovering the Festival of Shelters (vv. 13-17)
parts.note: The next day the family leaders studied further and found the command to live for a week in shelters made of branches, recalling how Israel lived in temporary dwellings after leaving Egypt. The remark that nothing like it had happened since Joshua's time probably means it had never been kept with this much joy and by everyone together, since earlier celebrations of this festival are recorded.

parts.label: Reading every day (v. 18)
parts.note: The Law asked for a public reading at this festival only once every seven years, so reading it every day went beyond what was required. The festival closed with a special gathering on the eighth day, as the Law directed.

think: Have you ever heard something true about yourself that brought grief and relief at the same time, and what helped you move from one to the other?
